Ranges of integers and disjoint unions

Source: R/sets-range.R
Range.Rd

Range(stop) or Range(start, stop, step) is the set of integers start, start + step, ... before stop, in SymPy's canonical form (the stop moves to the first value past the last element, and an empty range is Range(0, 0, 1)). It supports membership with contains(), intersections with intervals, ranges and the integers, and sequence_terms(r, n) for its first elements. DisjointUnion(...) tags the elements of each set with the set's index, like SymPy.

Usage

Range(start, stop = NULL, step = 1)

DisjointUnion(...)

Arguments

start, stop, step

Integers or infinities.

...

Sets.

Value

A set.

Examples

Range(1, 10, 3)
#> Range(1, 10, 3)
contains(Range(1, 10, 3), 7)
#> [1] TRUE
Intersection(Range(1, 10, 3), Interval(3, 8))
#> Range(4, 10, 3)
